devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"You shall not steal." This command protects what rightfully belongs to another person — their property, their possessions, the fruit of their labour. But stealing wears many faces. It can be as obvious as robbery, or as subtle as cheating at work, underpaying a worker, dodging honest debts, cutting corners, or taking credit that belongs to someone else. Anywhere we take what is not ours, we break this command.

Underneath stealing lies a deeper problem: discontentment, and a failure to trust God as our provider. When we truly believe that God will supply what we need, we are freed from the grasping fear that drives us to take what belongs to others. Theft says, "God has not given me enough, so I will seize it myself." Faith says, "My Father knows what I need and will provide."

The gospel not only stops us from stealing; it transforms us into generous givers. Paul told thieves not merely to quit stealing but to start working and sharing with those in need (Eph 4:28). That is the beautiful reversal Christ works in us — from taking to giving. Jesus, though He was rich, became poor for our sake so that we might be made rich in Him (2 Cor 8:9). When your heart rests in His provision, open hands come naturally. Let Him make you honest, hardworking, and generous.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are there subtle ways I take what is not rightfully mine — time, credit, honesty?
- Do I trust God as my provider, or does fear drive me to grasp?
- How might God be calling me to move from taking to generous giving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for providing all I truly need. Free me from every subtle form of stealing, and make me honest, hardworking, and generous, reflecting the generosity of Jesus who gave everything for me. Amen.
